proposals.premise: Three records share one bend, so a chronological archive can expose relationships while labeling the unverified photographer, changed river shape, east abutment and public steps.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows the three dated records in one horizontal sequence beside a source panel; phone stacks the same sequence, with source and uncertainty labels sharing each card.
proposals.move: Select a record card to expand its photo, scan or audio player in place; the source, transcript and related-record links appear directly below.
proposals.tradeoff: Chronology makes finding and comparing records immediate, but the audio receives no special prominence.

proposals.premise: Assume visitors do not recognize the bend across eras; because its shape changed, organize the experience around evidence fragments rather than a stable map.
proposals.opening: Desktop opens with the 2025 sound player beside the transcript and three tactile record tabs; phone shows the player first, with transcript and tabs sharing the next screen.
proposals.move: Press a record tab to replace the evidence pane with the 1932 photo or 1978 scan; its location note, uncertainty and links to the other records appear underneath.
proposals.tradeoff: Sound creates a slower, present-day entry into comparison, but visitors seeking the oldest record need an extra selection.
